study.question: After stabilizing auxiliary reduction, does the native occupied-row-centered auxiliary product-context cotangent improve click AUC because of its sign, both with the batch-mean component removed and retained?
study.hypothesis: The example-specific centered transfer C carries beneficial directional information beyond generic transfer energy. Native C should outperform -C, and G=M+C should outperform M-C, under the same collected FP64 topology. Recent half-swap controls support assignment dependence but do not identify sign utility. Earlier sign contrasts were undermined by an allegedly equivalent replay that changed the ordering; their evidence is provisional. No click-gradient alignment or parameter-space orthogonality mechanism is asserted.

nearest_work.difference: Nearest local implementation is the full/centered by aligned/half-swap FP64 collection factorial. Retain its forward model and collection topology; now freeze example assignment and reverse C with M absent/present.

This repeats the earlier sign/reflection question through the later stable aggregate FP64 reduction, with common native bridges. It is a numerical attribution follow-up, not a new architectural contribution.

study.proposed_difference: Extend the collected auxiliary VJP with one non-tensor centered-orientation argument. Let G be ordered cart+fav+buy context cotangents on occupied-history rows, M the repeated occupied-row mean, and C=G-M. Four standalone cells return C, -C, G, or M-C before the inherited single cast. All cells compute the same components and both signs; aligned assignment is frozen. Full native returns G directly, avoiding a C+M cancellation round trip. These explicit surrogate-backward controls are not derivatives of the identity forward or alternative scalar losses; private parameters retain ordinary BCE gradients.
predictions: Host fixed-state forward probabilities, scalar loss, private task gradients, module state and RNG agree across all four variants; only the auxiliary product-context input VJP differs.

FP64 occupied-row sums of C and -C are approximately zero; G and M-C have the same occupied-row mean M and the same total row-space Frobenius norm up to roundoff. Empty-history cotangents are zero in every cell.
Native replay C reproduces g3-r0043-centered_aligned64 and native G reproduces g3-r0043-full_aligned64 under the predeclared replay gate.
Conditional on those gates, Delta_absent=AUC(C)-AUC(-C)>0 and Delta_retained=AUC(G)-AUC(M-C)>0. Predict signs, not exact gain sizes or significance.
No new inference operators or parameters; measured training cost stays close to recent 360-375 second complete units, subject to host verification.
falsifiers: A nonpositive native-minus-reversed click AUC contrast after valid replay gates falsifies beneficial native direction in that mean stratum for this seed.
If the new native bridges fail fixed-state identity or differ from historical native AUC by more than 1e-6, the mechanism interpretation is unresolved regardless of apparent improvement.
Changed forward probabilities, private parameter gradients, running buffers, masking or click direct-path gradients at fixed state invalidate the intended contrast.
Failure of empty-history zeroing, component algebra or numerical norm/mean tolerances invalidates the intervention implementation.
An effect confined to one mean stratum does not support mean-independent direction utility; equality after independent authorized repetition would refute reproducible utility.
alternative_explanations: Row-space equal norm does not imply equal per-example norm or equal embedding-parameter norm after repeated-ID accumulation.
Adagrad state, shared-field frequency and subsequent parameter trajectories interact with the prescribed VJP.
One frozen seed and adaptively chosen validation contrasts; no independent repetition or population significance.
BF16 upstream arithmetic and downstream sparse accumulation remain unchanged; FP64 only stabilizes the specified reduction.
The batch-global mean mixes users; centering is an optimization diagnostic and has no claimed production causal meaning.
Equal row-space transfer energy can produce different frequency-weighted embedding updates and adaptive preconditioning.
Sign reversal can destabilize auxiliary private learning indirectly over training, even with identical private gradients at the same state.
Offline delayed-feedback visibility and category/brand-matched auxiliary labels limit transfer to online systems.

trajectory_summary.observation: Joint click AUC 0.6684573079 versus click-only/context-blocked 0.6678548721; rolled labels 0.6674639466. This motivates useful context transfer, with only single-seed support.
Single auxiliary-task, pair and scaled-transfer attempts did not exceed the joint reference (e.g. cart+fav 0.6681492093 and joint x2/3 0.6681406600). Do not infer every task independently helps.

Product-only 0.6684156160 exceeded residual-only 0.6676246608; incumbent joint-aligned 0.6684738720 remains higher than recent FP64 product-only variants. This attribution suite is not a claim of a new best model.

Earlier native C 0.6683622090 exceeded reversed C 0.6677870949 and native G 0.6684156160 exceeded M-C 0.6677229688. But an algebraic C replay fell to 0.6676314513 while a -C replay scored 0.6677697258, reversing that comparison. This counterevidence prevents treating the earlier sign result as established.

FP32 task/aggregate collection scored 0.6674577110/0.6674397049, whereas both FP64 cells scored exactly 0.6682972490. This supports reduction sensitivity as an implementation concern; deterministic agreement is not independent repetition.
FP64 C/G/M/blocked scored 0.6682972490/0.6683663357/0.6677131772/0.6678548721. Mean-only failed to explain the useful transfer. Removing M changes magnitude, so this is not a pure directional result.

C aligned-minus-swapped=0.0002294576672542 and G aligned-minus-swapped=0.0004396116330854. Both native outcomes replay round42 exactly. Assignment dependence survived this implementation bridge, but sign utility remains to be tested in that stable topology.
